description: Safe Unix, Linux, macOS, and shell command workflows.

capabilities: Turn plain-language tasks into safe, copy-ready Unix and shell commands
Explain and debug Bash, zsh, POSIX shell commands, pipelines, quoting, and redirection
Distinguish Linux, macOS/BSD, GNU, Bash, zsh, and POSIX command behavior
Preview risky file, permission, process, package, and system changes before execution
Write and review shell scripts with argument checks, cleanup, errors, and safe quoting
Handle find, grep, sed, awk, xargs, sorting, and bulk file operations safely
Work with CSV, TSV, encodings, and command-line data preparation without corrupting data
Diagnose shell-script failures from errors, traces, exit codes, and command output
Provide OS-appropriate package-manager, PATH, shell, and environment guidance
Use current primary docs for shell, utility, GNU/BSD, macOS, and package-manager differences
defaultPrompt: Write a safe shell command for this task.
Explain and fix this Unix or shell command.
Convert this workflow into a safe Bash or zsh script.
interface.longDescription: Unix Copilot helps you write, understand, debug, and safely run shell commands and scripts across Linux and macOS. It can translate plain-language tasks into copy-ready commands, explain pipes and redirection, troubleshoot shell scripts, handle files and text safely, prepare CSV and delimited data, and provide OS-appropriate package and environment guidance. It distinguishes POSIX, Bash, zsh, GNU, BSD/macOS, and Linux behavior, uses dry-runs and validation for risky operations, and avoids unsafe patterns such as unverified recursive deletion, broad permission changes, secret exposure, and brittle filename parsing.

name: unix-copilot
